question_text: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?

why_it_matters.text: Thomas Jefferson, then 33 years old, wrote the Declaration of Independence in a few weeks in a rented Philadelphia room. His words — 'all men are created equal,' the right to 'life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness' — became the founding promise of the United States. America has spent its whole history trying to live up to that promise.

fun_fact.text: Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration at age 33. Fifty years later, on July 4, 1826 — the EXACT 50th anniversary of the Declaration — Jefferson and John Adams both died on the same day. Adams was the last to go; his final words: 'Thomas Jefferson survives.' But Jefferson had died hours earlier.
